_comment: The 14 research dimensions. Structure, not scores (design v2 §3.3). Each dimension is a research-checklist item and a dossier section. 'cost_tagged' drives grounded_claim's stricter cost rules (spec §3.1.3). 'tracks' = which evidence pools research it; 'look_for' = per-track scoping hints. Case-agnostic: no domain baked in.

dimensions.name: Strategic differentiation / moat
dimensions.question: Does owning this build competitive advantage or proprietary data that compounds?

BUILD: whether the capability is core IP or a commodity
evidence that building creates a durable moat or compounding advantage
BUY: how far commercial options commoditize this capability
what differentiation, if any, survives after buying

dimensions.name: Proprietary-data generation
dimensions.question: Does building this generate data no competitor can replicate?

BUILD: whether owning the implementation produces proprietary data exhaust
whether that data flywheel compounds over time
BUY: who owns the data a vendor processes
whether the vendor captures or restricts use of data generated through it

dimensions.name: Total cost — build
dimensions.question: Engineering salaries x time, infra, and the opportunity cost of what those engineers are not building.

BUILD: dated engineering-effort estimates for comparable builds
opportunity cost framing (what the team is not building instead)

dimensions.name: Total cost — maintenance (the bloat curve)
dimensions.question: What does upkeep cost in year 2, 3, 5 as it accretes features and tech debt?

BUILD: dated evidence on long-run maintenance burden and tech-debt accretion
the year-2/3/5 upkeep curve for self-built or self-hosted systems
BUY: residual integration/operational maintenance left to the buyer after purchase

dimensions.name: Total cost — buy (short + long term)
dimensions.question: License + integration + per-seat scaling + price-escalation risk at renewal.

BUY: whether pricing is gated behind sales contact (state as a finding, not a gap)

dimensions.name: Time-to-value
dimensions.question: Time to a working capability for each path.

BUILD: dated estimates of time-to-first-working-version for comparable builds
BUY: typical onboarding/integration time to production for the commercial option

dimensions.name: Resource & talent availability
dimensions.question: Do we have the engineers/skills, or must we hire?

BUILD: scarcity of the skills the build requires
BUY: skills needed to integrate/operate the bought option (lighter, but non-zero)

dimensions.name: Reversibility / switching cost
dimensions.question: How expensive is it to unwind this decision later? (The dimension most frameworks omit.)

BUILD: how locked-in a self-built/self-hosted choice becomes (data, ops, expertise)
BUY: contract lock-in, data-export/portability, migration cost away from the vendor

dimensions.name: Data ownership / sensitivity / compliance
dimensions.question: Where does data live? Regulatory exposure? Vendor data-handling risk?

BUILD: data-residency/control achievable when self-hosting or building
BUY: vendor data-handling posture, certifications, sub-processors, residency options

dimensions.name: Customization need vs. availability
dimensions.question: How much must it bend to our workflow, and can each path deliver that?

BUILD: the degree of customization a build can achieve (full, but costly)
BUY: configurability / API surface / extensibility of the commercial option (this gates buy-then-extend)

dimensions.name: Focus / core-value alignment
dimensions.question: Does doing this ourselves distract from the company's core value?

BUILD: whether building pulls scarce focus away from the company's core value
BUY: whether buying lets the team stay on its core value

dimensions.name: Portfolio reuse & amortization
dimensions.question: Can this be built once and shared across N companies? (The Emergence multiplier.)
dimensions.note: Dormant in MVP (single-need; no Portfolio Memory). Survives as structure; activated by the Portfolio Memory Service in Target (target-architecture §B7). Research does not chase this dimension in the MVP.

dimensions.name: Vendor viability / lock-in risk
dimensions.question: Is the vendor (or OSS project) durable? Acquisition / EOL / abandonment risk?

BUILD: health of the OSS projects a build/adopt path depends on (maintenance cadence, governance, bus factor)
BUY: vendor durability signals: funding, traction, acquisition/EOL risk

dimensions.name: Integration complexity
dimensions.question: Cost to wire into existing (often legacy, underinvested) stacks.

BUILD: effort to integrate a self-built component into the existing stack
BUY: available connectors/APIs/SDKs and the integration effort for the commercial option
